subject: Post-call: Acme context-length & token-volume pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Acme context-length & token-volume pricing follow-up

Hi Sam — great to meet you and the team earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call so we can align on a pricing profile and target economics: 

Call recap (short):
- Primary use case: document understanding + long-form Q&A for customer support knowledge base and case transcripts.
- Expected workload mix: batch ingestion for indexing + interactive chat for agents.
- Key ops need: 99.9% availability for chat, regional (US) serving, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Requesting confirmation on the usage profile you shared so we can finalize unit economics:
- Avg prompt tokens per request: ~400 tokens (includes ~200 token system+context + ~200 token user prompt)
- Avg completion (output) tokens per request: ~800 tokens (longer summary mode)
- Estimated interactive requests/day: 12k -> ~360k/month active requests
- Bulk ingestion (embedding + chunking): ~1.2B input tokens/month (one-time large import in month 1, then steady-state smaller batches)
- Context-length needs: majority of interactive traffic needs 32k context for multi-doc context + some cases requiring 128k for large-case transcripts (roughly 5% of requests).

Attachments: I attached a sample_usage_profile.csv with the breakdown you gave and our preliminary pricing workbook (redwood_pricing_calc.xlsx).

Pricing questions / ask: 
1) Can you confirm the monthly active interactive requests and the 1.2B ingestion token estimate?
2) Do you have a target $/1M tokens (or target monthly spend range) for us to optimize toward? You mentioned a procurement budget range on the call — repeating here so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted.
3) For context-length, please confirm percentage split of 8k vs 32k vs 128k needed in steady state. We noted ~70% 8k/32k (split internal), 25% 32k, 5% 128k as a working assumption.

Next steps on our side when you confirm the numbers:
- We’ll run a unit-econ calc and provide 3 pricing options (Hosted pay-as-you-go, Committed Dedicated baseline, and a Hybrid with fallbacks) with per-1M token rates and expected monthly bill.
- Provide SOC2 + security pack and a procurement checklist for your team.
- Schedule follow-up with Rafael (solutions architect) for a short profiling session on any heavy 128k cases.

Proposed next meeting: 30 minutes this week for Rafael to walk through the 128k examples and confirm serialization/fragmentation strategy. I’m available Wed/Thu afternoons PT.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme context-length & token-volume pricing follow-up

Thanks Marissa — great notes and exactly what we need to move forward. Confirming the numbers & a few clarifications: 

- Interactive requests: we expect closer to 10k/day initially (300k/month), ramping to 20k/day by Q4 if pilot is successful.
- Avg tokens: your averages look right. Our engineering lead measured a sample of chat sessions: prompt ~380 tokens avg, completion ~760 tokens avg. Good to use 400/800 as conservative numbers for pricing.
- Ingestion: the 1.2B initial import is correct; steady-state monthly ingestion will be ~150M tokens.
- Context split (steady state): 60% 8k, 35% 32k, 5% 128k. The 128k requests are large-case transcripts from legal/finance reviews (low volume but latency tolerant).
- Budget target: procurement wants to target ~$1,500 - $3,000 / 1M tokens equivalent for the interactive use (we realize larger-scale committed pricing is different); their anchor is $2,000 / 1M tokens. For embeddings/ingestion the unit economics should be lower (we can discuss separate rates).

Procurement note: we’ll need an initial estimate of hosted vs committed spend to decide if we go dedicated. If Redwood can show a committed discounted baseline that hits ~$1,200 - $1,600 /1M tokens for the interactive workload at our scale, procurement will likely recommend Dedicated.

Sam

Sam Liu
Director of Product
Acme Corp
sam.liu@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Liu <sam.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme context-length & token-volume pricing follow-up

Sam — thanks for the clear confirmation and the budget anchor, that’s super helpful. Next steps from our side: 

1) Rafael and I will build a short unit-economics sheet showing three scenarios:
   - Hosted (PAYG): list per-1M token rates for prompt/completion and embeddings with a sample monthly bill at 300k and 1.2B ingestion assumptions.
   - Committed Dedicated (12/24-month): discount tiers that aim for your procurement target range ($1,200 - $1,600 /1M tokens interactive) at the expected volume. We’ll show the breakpoint and committed spend required.
   - Hybrid: Dedicated baseline for interactive with burst to hosted for 128k cases to avoid overprovisioning.

2) We’ll explicitly model context-length cost delta (8k vs 32k vs 128k) — because memory and KV-cache sizing impacts per-token cost when requests hold larger contexts. Expect to see ~1.0x baseline for 8k, ~1.35x for 32k, ~1.9x-2.4x for 128k depending on batching/latency SLO.

3) Rafael will request a short profiling session (15-20 mins) this week to get an anonymized sample transcript for the 128k cases so we can validate serialization strategy. Rafael — are you available Wed 2pm PT / Thu 11am PT?

4) I’ll send the draft pricing workbook and a short one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated economics by EOD tomorrow.

If procurement has a target committed term (12 vs 24 months) please paste here so we can model scenarios.

Marissa

--

Action items:

- Nikhil: draft a short One-Pager for procurement that shows committed tiers (12m/24m) and expected savings vs Hosted. Include recommended committed spend to hit the $1,200/1M interactive target.
- Marissa: I’ll schedule the 15-20m profiling session with Sam and Rafael once Rafael confirms availability.

Marissa
